name: juman
why: A Japanese morphological analyser from Kyoto University, a rare piece of old NLP worth taking apart for its lattice-based segmentation.

brief.what_it_is: JUMAN is a Japanese morphological analyser from Kyoto University's Language Media Processing Lab. It takes Japanese text (UTF-8 since version 7.0) and splits it into morphemes, one per line, giving each token's surface form, reading, dictionary base form, part of speech and conjugation info, with an EOS line closing each sentence. The homepage's sample shows it handling informal and non-standard spellings such as ビミョーだ, ありがとー and 行きたぁぁぁい. The executable is juman, and it reads from stdin, e.g. juman < sample.txt.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it was built to give many researchers studying computational analysis of Japanese a common morphological analysis tool, and that school grammar is poorly suited to computers, so the grammar definitions and the connection rules between words can be changed easily by the user.
brief.how_it_works: The fetched pages do not describe the segmentation algorithm; the 'lattice-based' framing in the scout notes is not confirmed by anything I read. The repository tree does show makemat (source for connectivity rules), makeint (dictionary conversion) and makepat (a Patricia database), and the sample output carries auto-acquired tags such as 自動獲得:Wikipedia and 既知語帰着, which suggests dictionary lookup plus connection-rule scoring, but I did not verify that from the text.

brief.install_notes: Requirements from the homepage: a Unix-like system or Microsoft Windows XP or later, at least 100MB of memory and 200MB of free disk. Building from source is the standard autoconf sequence: ./configure, make, make install, with ./autogen.sh first if building from git. The GitHub INSTALL file I opened is only the generic GNU autoconf text, with nothing JUMAN-specific. Windows users get an installer for 7.0 (32-bit and 64-bit) from the homepage. Perl bindings ship in the package under perl/. The Windows Perl route uses an old Active Perl 5.8.8 module installer. Python users are pointed to PyKNP.
brief.standout: Most morphological analysers are built around a fixed school-grammar tagset; JUMAN was designed so users can edit the grammar and connection rules, and the 7.0 changes add automatic recognition of onomatopoeia, long-vowel marks and small kana, plus dictionaries auto-acquired from web text and Wikipedia. The homepage's sample output shows it recognising colloquial forms like ありがとー and 行きたぁぁぁい as long-vowel variants of standard words.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage's most recent release entry is Ver.7.01, published 2014-12-22, with a bug fix for long-vowel insertion. The homepage itself was last modified 2021-12-22. The GitHub repository (ku-nlp/juman) exists and its README is current in layout, but I did not see a commit date, so I cannot say how active development is.
brief.caveats: The homepage is in Japanese, and most of its text is navigation, so the English description here comes from the homepage's Japanese prose plus the English GitHub README. The GitHub README is thin and sends readers to doc/manual.pdf, which I did not open. Windows binaries exist only for 7.0, and the Windows Perl instructions reference a very old Active Perl. The homepage lists Juman++ and KNP as separate tools on the same page, so readers may want to know which one they are after. The lattice mechanism mentioned in the scout notes is not confirmed by the pages I read. Licensing was not confirmed; the GitHub repo has a COPYING file, which I did not open.
